checks.diagnosis: The prompt allows cuts that split off a clause’s assertion from an immediate negation or negative determiner, producing a fragment that alone asserts the opposite of the whole sentence.
checks.evidence: ['de_de_1339','de_de_1034','de_de_601','de_de_1599','de_de_694'] — each case shows the policy kept a cut immediately before a German negation token (e.g. 'nicht'/'kein') or a span whose immediate continuation negates the earlier claim, producing a high contra.
checks.type_predicate: Markers that occur immediately before a German negation token (nicht, kein, nie) or a negative determiner.

edit.text: Do not cut immediately before a negation token (nicht/kein/nie); mark such positions as forbidden (must-not-cut).

orders.diagnosis: The prompt fails to prefer cuts that preserve whole noun phrases, instead splitting inside noun-heavy spans and hurting cohesion when pieces are translated separately.
orders.evidence: ['de_de_1034','de_de_725','de_de_441','de_de_928'] — in each case the better segmentation puts the noun-head together with its modifiers (target moves the cut later to keep the NP intact).
orders.type_predicate: Pairs of candidate markers that both fall inside the same contiguous noun phrase (sequence of determiners/adjectives/nouns before a noun head).

edit.text: When two markers lie inside the same noun phrase, prefer the later cut that preserves the noun head with its modifiers (do not split the NP).
